summary: The chronological-dispatch gate landed asserting rule text that was never committed, so master was red on every clean checkout while the author's working tree was green

action: Ship the contract text the gate asserts (the three contract documents now declare the dependency-ordered rule)
Count and report each non-conforming contract document independently instead of through a shared counter

evidence.note: the fix that made a clean checkout green again

title: Prove a gate against the committed tree, never the working tree: reconstruct the files it asserts on from the merge commit and run it there

remediation: add a gate-proof step that reconstructs the asserted files from the merge commit and runs the check there, so a dirty tree can never manufacture a pass
title: Every new gate ships a clean-checkout proof

summary: Issue #148 was reported complete with passing test evidence while every file it claimed to deliver was still untracked; nothing had shipped

action: Ship the work the completion report claimed: the leaderboard session registry and its suite
Confirm every claimed file with `git ls-files --error-unmatch <file>` before reporting an issue done

evidence.note: the delivery the misreported claim had not shipped

title: Work that is not committed does not exist: a passing run in the working tree is not evidence of delivery

summary: Two lanes worked one issue in parallel and shipped a byte-identical 53-line change to the three contract documents; one merge was pure waste

action: Record and validate a single claim before work starts, so an in-flight issue is locked and a second claim fails loudly

evidence.note: PR #159 landed the claim gate for issue #157

title: A rule that exists only in prose is advisory: concurrent lanes need a claim lock, not a declaration gate

remediation: publish the lane claim to the steering channel when it is taken, so two lanes on one issue see the overlap before a pull request is opened
title: Make lane overlap visible at claim time, not at merge time

summary: The claim audit retroactively failed a completed issue ("#139: claimed after it was closed") because the replay compared a historical claim event against the present board snapshot

action: Treat a released claim as finished history: the closed-issue and milestone-frontier rules apply only to a claim still live at audit time

evidence.note: PR #172 fixed the replay in governance/dispatch/claims.py

title: A frontier is a point-in-time property: never recompute a historical decision from today's snapshot

summary: The claim gate reported closed issue #139 as the eligible frontier from a board snapshot that was 19 minutes old; the reader consumed stale data as truth because it had no freshness rule

action: Add a snapshot-staleness check to the claim gate and store claims conflict-free, so an answer derived from a stale snapshot is refused rather than returned

remediation: state the age a point-in-time artifact may reach before it is refused, and read the timestamp the artifact already carries (issue #170)
title: A snapshot's timestamp is part of its meaning

summary: The AgentConsole go-live was designed against agent-orchestrator's own GCP Cloud Run pipeline (epic #607) and published to the operator as 'one deploy away', while the fleet's live-hosting contract (shared-frontend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md, owner directive 2026-09-04) fixes the remote shared-services cluster as the only live host and had deliberately removed the Cloud Run config; the deployment contract was documented in the peer modules the whole time

action: Scavenge and declare the AgentConsole hosting contract from the peer modules (shared-frontend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md + contrib/shared-services, shared-services infra) and hand the run half to its owners as a direction issue

evidence.note: AgentConsole lane A: the shared-services hosting handoff + a bootable image

remediation: Before choosing a host for any go-live, read the peer modules' deployment contracts and the owner directives they encode (shared-frontend docs/DEPLOYMENT.md; shared-services infra) and scavenge the project ids, service accounts, secret names and edge config from them; a documented hosting contract is an input, never an external boundary.
title: A deployment contract documented in a peer module is an input, not an unknown boundary

summary: Epic #607's go-live was declared for months and never exercised: the declarations asserted nothing was live, and the console image recipe had never been built (its only builder was the retired Cloud Run route), so a defect inside the artifact - portal/Dockerfile installed PyYAML but not cryptography, exiting 1 at boot - was invisible until the go-live ran.

action: Add a binding, self-proving gate for the AgentConsole hosting contract (scripts/check-agentconsole-hosting.sh, registered in scripts/verify.sh) that asserts the image recipe, the overlay, the together-promoted surfaces, the live-host declaration and the fail-closed env contract offline, and mutates one property per rule on every run

title: declared is not exercised: a declared artifact (an image recipe, an overlay, a contract doc) is unfalsifiable until a control reads or runs it - give every declaration a gate that can fail, or it drifts from the tree silently

summary: A shared 16 GiB /tmp tmpfs filled to 100 % (one 14.8 GB scratch log no process held) and a redirected write on the full filesystem failed as a 0-byte file, so a gh issue create --body-file reported success with an EMPTY body: no gate measured free space, no ceiling bounded a single scratch file, and no artifact was read back before it was trusted

action: Deliver the machine-checkable infra-limit guard (free-space floor and used-percent ceiling, orphan-hog ceiling, read-back write rule) plus the sandbox and ephemeral-storage contract linked from AGENTS.md, and register it in the gate of record

remediation: keep scripts/check-infra-limits.sh wired into the gate of record and extend it when a new shared resource or a new silent-failure mode appears (issue #729)
title: An infra limit is not a limit until a gate measures it

summary: Two agents can be dispatched onto the same work with no arbiter: the A2A transport moves messages and the claim ledger records per-issue claims, but no rule decides between two claimants and no refusal is published to the loser (measured: zero arbitrat* vocabulary anywhere in fleet/, and INC-0003 shipped a byte-identical 53-line change twice)

action: Give the agent-to-agent dispatch path one arbitration rule: a single arbiter per target, a refusal (not a warning) for a second claimant, and the refusal published to the caller so the loser is attributed and stopped

remediation: name in one place the rule that decides between two claimants and the verdict the loser receives, instead of assuming agents coordinate (issue #726)
title: An agent-to-agent path without an arbiter is a broadcast, not a protocol

summary: Gates stacked on one shared box: 3-4 concurrent make verify runs and eight gate processes at load ~85-107, with long runs SIGTERM'd by a neighbouring lane's interrupt so a run died at the same step regardless of the change under test and had to be re-run to earn its evidence; scripts/verify.sh takes no lock (grep for flock/gatelock: 0 hits) and fleet/gatelock.py does not exist

action: Add a gate lock so one gate of record runs per worktree and a second invocation waits or is refused by name, making a stacked run a declared outcome instead of an accident

remediation: take a lock in anything that consumes the whole box and name the holder when it refuses, so the failure stops presenting as someone else's flaky test (issue #724)
title: A gate is a resource claim, not just a script

summary: An uncapped retry loop re-invoked make verify after each termination and stacked 137+ verify.sh processes from two orphaned worktrees (68 and 69 copies each) with no driver process remaining, so the storm self-perpetuated through the make -> verify.sh fork chain and read as 'the box is just busy'; no cap and no attempt ledger existed (fleet/runaway.py absent)

action: Cap redispatch with an attempt ledger, a terminal refusal when the cap is reached, and a refusal that names the dispatcher, so a retry storm cannot outlive its driver

remediation: cap attempts by count and time, keep an attempt ledger, and refuse terminally naming the dispatcher rather than the process (issue #723)
title: A retry loop must be bounded, and its bound must be visible

summary: Gates that no gate invokes: check-negative-controls.sh, check-policy-schema.sh and check-pr-contract.sh have zero references in scripts/verify.sh and check-drift.sh appears there only inside a comment, so the gate of record is missing three checks it is recorded as having; coverage is opt-in via an explicit checks=() array and the unwired class grew from 0 to 8 in one day when EPIC #499 landed six at once

action: Refuse a newly delivered scripts/check-*.sh that no gate file invokes by path, naming the path, and never grandfather it into the coverage baseline (a baseline row for a newly delivered artifact is refused, and stale rows fail)

remediation: register every delivered check by path from a gate file, and let the delivered-vs-invoked gap be found by a gate rather than a review (issue #725)
title: Delivery is not coverage: an artifact no gate invokes is inert

summary: The committed board snapshot carries generated_at but has no trigger and no refresh path in this repository (Makefile has only board-gate:, governance/board/cli.py has no capture verb, governance/dispatch/snapshot.py has no refresh function, fleet/cron.py never mentions the board), so consumers resolve through a frontier that stops at issue #559 while the work in flight is EPIC #708 and its #723-#729 children: a legitimate issue origin is refused as origin-unresolved and an honest baseline deferral cannot be recorded

action: Make the board snapshot refresh a scheduled or evented action rather than a manual one, and have each consumer state the age it tolerates and refuse (or warn) beyond it, so staleness is measured instead of discovered

remediation: trigger the refresh from the events that invalidate the snapshot and state the tolerated age in every consumer: a timestamp plus a tolerance without a trigger turns a data-staleness bug into a stopped lane (issue #727)
title: A committed snapshot needs a trigger, or its freshness rule becomes an outage
